dedupe_keys.name: a worldwide historical dam failure s database

description: This database compiles 3,861 historical dam failures worldwide, assembled from 196 references by Mayari Bernard-Garcia and Tew-Fik Mahdi at Polytechnique Montréal; the authors describe it as the largest compilation of dam failures recorded to date (17 February 2020). It includes failures regardless of dam type (man-made, tailings, temporary or natural dams), structure (concrete, embankment and others), failure mode (piping, overtopping and others) or dam properties, and records up to 45 variables per case where available, such as dam height, reservoir capacity, breach dimensions and failure hydrographs. The aim was to standardise the collection of historical failure data and give researchers and dam owners a shared basis for hydrology, hydraulics and dam safety work. The file is an Excel workbook with filters and pivot tables, deposited on Borealis, the Canadian Dataverse, with a bilingual English and French description; version 1 was distributed on 6 August 2020 (production 7 March 2019). Access: free download under a CC0 dedication with additional terms given on the record. Caveats: coverage and attribute completeness vary with the historical sources, duplicates and uncertain cases are flagged for users to verify, the file has not been updated since 2020 although updates were promised, and tailings failures overlap with specialised tailings inventories. Simulation uses: estimating breach parameters and failure probabilities for dam-break hazard models, validating breach and inundation modelling, and informing emergency planning. Related records: the US National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams), Global Dam Watch (data-global-dam-watch-database) and HEC-RAS (model-hec-ras) for breach simulation.
